rv.q: Andrew Lloyd Webber is cool again.
Back on the terra fur-ma of a stage, this rebooted Cats repaired some of the reputational damage done by the Hollywood folly.
Lloyd Webber's score sounds great... Fendall's work is wonderful, including costumes and wigs that play attractive games with a gamut of textures.
McOnie clearly loves Cats but this production often doesn't feel very catty.
For me the first half of Drew McOnie's sleek production doesn't excite or register enough of an emotional connection.
It’s a visual feast with a hint of wildness that blends well with the darkening skies of the open-air theatre.
Really it’s a very decent production of a tuneful and idiosyncratic musical that just happens to have sold a kerchillion tickets back in the day.
McOnie's version is probably more pedestrian and safe than the drag/ballroom adaptation that recently wowed New York.
It is, in short, a purr-fect rebirth.
Fendall's costuming alone is worth making the trek for.
The oddest musical works its magic again.
Air Theatre production offers a sleek and modern take on a show that has now begun to show its age a little.
It is a wonderful experience for any lover of musical theatre, dance, and cats.
McOnie makes half a case for it with this hit-and-miss revival but doesn’t quite reach the Heaviside Layer before daybreak.
For the main part, it was fun. But I can't see any likelihood of this Jellicle troupe transferring to a West End cattery any time soon.
Even by musical theatre standards, the show is sluggish and too repetitive.

What Drew McOnie has created with this production is nothing short of sensational - truly awe-inspiring and a show that has just established himself as the front-runner to sweep the Olivier Awards next year.
I smiled my way through this production and there were moments of awe.
McOnie has done something properly beautiful.
This latest revival offers another interpretation of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s beloved musical performed in the idyllic setting of Regent’s Air Theatre.
Overall, this is probably one of my favourite productions which the Regent's Air Theatre has staged over the last few years.
There’s not a dustbin in sight in director and choreographer Drew McOnie’s sexed up, high-octane production that stirs and transfixes.
Melanie La Barrie also proves she can lead a cast as Old Deuteronomy who is ringleader for the only real plot you need to know.
Few musicals give movement, imagination and theatrical playfulness quite so much room to take over.
For those seeking a nostalgic return to one of musical theatre's most distinctive creations, this revival offers plenty of entertainment, even if it occasionally falls short of its full potential.

Its presentation is uneven and disjointed, and while there are components of this Cats revival which can be appreciated in isolation, McOnie’s vibrant choreography and Lloyd Webber’s classic score struggle to operate in harmony.
And that’s what makes Regent’s Park’s Theatre’s production passable in every sense of the word — it has a pass, but you can also pass on it.
This cat lands firmly on all four feet.
I left having fallen, at this late and unlikely stage, rather in love with it.
The first half, however, needs greater energy, spectacle, individuality and visual clarity.
Ultimately, the production feels surprisingly safe.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace Drew McOnie's bold, contemporary revival, praising its sleek choreography and outdoor setting. While some find the show inherently silly and structurally loose, most agree this production breathes fresh life into the divisive classic.
